newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila minister resigns amid row over land deal.
newsitem.headline: Manila minister resigns amid row over land deal.

text.p: Philippine Transportation and Communications Secretary Amado Lagdameo, the former head of a state agency now at the centre of a controversial land deal, has resigned, President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday.
Ramos told his weekly news conference he accepted Lagdameo's resignation effective on April 16.
Lagdameo's departure follows a long-running political row over the land deal between the Public Estates Authority (PEA) and privately-owned Amari Coastal Development Corp.
Amari is a joint venture between local property development firm Centennial City and Thai construction firm Ital-Thai Development Plc.
The deal, negotiated when Lagdameo was head of the PEA, involved the reclamation and development of 750 hectares (1,853 acres) of land forming part of the giant Manila Bay project.
Since last year, Senate president and opposition leader Ernesto Maceda has alleged the government entered into a disadvantageous deal, claiming the property was grossly underpriced.
The presidential palace has upheld the deal but ordered a renegotiation of certain of its provisions.

Lagdameo has not been accused of any wrongdoing but a presidential fact-finding committee recommended investigation of two former PEA officials and a government lawyer to determine if they had benefited from the contract.

Ramos said he had ordered the committee to submit its findings to the government ombudsman, or chief prosecutor, "with a listing of the details in regard to what are called administrative lapses." He did not elaborate.
Presidential Executive Secretary Ruben Torres said last week the he had directed the PEA to "clarify and renegotiate" the deal. A revised final agreement will be submitted to Ramos for approval.

Guoco Holdings (Phils) Inc, parent company of Centennial City, has defended the deal, saying its valuation of 1,250 pesos ($48) per square metre was based on appraisals made by three independent firms.
